chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not sit between the two prostrations with a full, deep sitting (i.e., do not sit fully upright and settled).

key_terms.إِقْعَاءً: A full, deep sitting posture (as opposed to a light, transitional sit)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to sit between the two prostrations in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between 'Iq'a' (sitting on the heels with an upright torso) and 'Tawarruk' or intermediate sitting, prescribing the latter for the interval between prostrations to maintain humility and continuity. In Shia fiqh, this ruling emphasizes the importance of distinct postures for different acts of worship, ensuring the transition between bowing and prostration is neither too abrupt nor too static, thereby preserving the spiritual focus of the prayer.
